view: This is a clinical-stage biotech whose quarterly release carries no new clinical readout. The 10-01 EADV data reset the story, and the stock has been base-building near 1.3x cash for four weeks. Since 10-01 there has been no 8-K, no clinical disclosure and no Lilly post-trial ruling I could find; EDGAR shows only an S-8 (10-20) and a passive 13G (11-10). The Q3 release will most likely restate the runway (into Q3 2028), ZENITH-AD progress, the ZENITH-AA start in early 2027, the Q1 2027 AD update and the TrialNet T1D study, with opex close to the Q2 run rate. All of that is in the price. What could move it is unforecastable from public traces: an accelerated timeline, FDA feedback on the single registrational AA study, a partnering remark, or a court ruling on Lilly's post-trial motions or on interest. The 20% short interest and 10 days to cover mean any positive surprise would move the stock more than a routine print. The call-rich skew and the floor near cash lean slightly the same way. Neither of those is evidence about the release itself. I hold no directional view worth acting on.

recommendation.reason: A Q3 print with no scheduled data has no visible line that the price fails to hold. Every disclosed item (cash, runway, trial timelines) is restated from the Q2 release and the EADV update, and nothing new has surfaced since 10-01. The crowded short sets the size of a reaction, not its direction.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A new, dated program disclosure in the release or on the call: FDA alignment on a single AA registrational trial, a ZENITH enrollment pull-forward, a partnership, or a court ruling on the Lilly award or interest. Any of these into 20% short interest would make it an upside call; a pushed timeline or a higher burn guide would make it a downside one.

self_critique: The case for a move I am not calling: a 20% short base in a stock near 1.3x cash, with no news for six weeks, can squeeze hard on any constructive call commentary, such as FDA alignment on the AA Phase 3 or a firm Q1 2027 AD date. Management has an incentive to talk up after a 45% drawdown, so the upside tail is fatter than the downside. Against that, the last two prints moved -3.8% and -1.8%, and the shorts held through the crash, which suggests a conviction or hedged short rather than a fragile one. That keeps me near 50.
